description: Renovate keeps the sha256-pinned release downloads in the workflows current (gitleaks,
actionlint, osv-scanner, the Codacy coverage reporter), which Dependabot cannot see, and the
container images pinned as tag@sha256: the fuzz image's base (.clusterfuzzlite/Dockerfile), the
images of this repository's two ClusterFuzzLite actions (.github/actions/cflite-*/action.yml) and
the Scorecard action's image recorded in scorecard.yml. For an image it proposes the tag's new
digest when the tag moves, never another tag: the Scorecard tag follows the action's version,
which Dependabot updates.
Everything else stays with Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml, which has no docker entry), so
the two never propose the same update. Renovate adds the managerFilePatterns set here to each
built-in manager's own (which read every workflow and every Dockerfile or Containerfile), so
packageRules turn the github-actions manager off for the workflows and the dockerfile manager
off for the add-ons' Containerfiles.
Each pinned download is marked in its step's env with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=owner/repo`
line directly above the VERSION (the release tag) and SHA256 lines. The
github-release-attachments datasource finds the asset the current sha256 belongs to and
proposes the new tag together with that asset's new sha256. A pinned image in a workflow is an
*IMAGE: 'name:tag@sha256:...' line under `# renovate: datasource=docker`.
The registries these images live on (gcr.io, ghcr.io) give Renovate no release timestamp, and
with the default timestamp-required a digest update would wait on minimumReleaseAge forever, so
docker updates are raised without one (Renovate docs, minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour).
tests/unit/part19.py and part242.py gate that every pin is matched and that each manager reads
only its own files.
The add-ons' pins live in the add-on catalog's source, panel/addon_images/catalog.json, which
tools/sign-catalog.sh signs for panels to fetch, so an add-on update needs no panel update. The
built add-ons' Containerfiles declare their ARGs with no default: the panel and the image scan pass
the catalog's values, so Renovate changes the catalog alone.
The pins: B3's source, the newest FMSMITH91/big-brother-bot
release tag and its commit (git-tags; master is
the next version in development, so it is never proposed),
IW4MAdmin's release, the newest RaidMax/IW4M-Admin release tag and the sha256 of the archive attached to
it (a custom datasource reads GitHub's releases
API, where each asset carries its sha256 digest: github-release-attachments maps an asset by the tag's
text, and IW4MAdmin's tags end in -prerelease while its archives do not, so it would find none), the
base of the IW4MAdmin image, the digest of mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 (its catalog base),
the B3 image's base, the digest of
python:3.15-slim (its catalog base;
both bases written by digest alone, as podman takes them, so the tag Renovate follows is the manager's
currentValueTemplate), and BlueMap's image, the digest of its `v5` tag (a new 5.x release, never
a new major one). All five are checked daily (packageRules). The B3 image's Python
dependencies (panel/addon_images/b3/requirements.txt, pip-compile's lock of requirements.in)
stay with Dependabot, like every other pip lockfile here: Renovate runs no pip manager.
The websites' pins live in the same catalog (sites): the PHP, Node.js, WordPress, wp-cli, Valkey,
nginx-unprivileged and cloudflared images, the tunnel image's Debian base, the page cache build's two Caddy
images, each by digest, and the npm the Node.js image installs. Each image keeps the tag of its supported
series (php:8.3-apache, node:22-bookworm-slim, valkey:9-alpine and so on), which the manager rebuilds from the
catalog's own keys and versions (currentValueTemplate), so a digest update never moves to another PHP,
Node.js or Valkey major; cloudflared's tag is its version and moves with it, and npm moves within its
major. WordPress's version is not Renovate's: the catalog holds one version for its three images, so
.github/workflows/site-app-versions.yml moves it, with the one-click apps' releases (version, url and
the archive's sha256, which Renovate cannot compute). tests/unit/part314.py gates that every websites pin is
matched once, by the tag the image really has.

customManagers.description: Workflow release downloads pinned by tag and sha256
Workflow container images pinned by tag and digest
The B3 add-on's source: FMSMITH91/big-brother-bot's newest release tag, pinned by tag and commit, in the add-on catalog
The IW4MAdmin add-on's release: RaidMax/IW4M-Admin's newest release tag and its archive's sha256, in the add-on catalog
The IW4MAdmin add-on image's base: the digest of mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0, in the add-on catalog
The BlueMap add-on's image: the digest of its v5 tag, in the add-on catalog
The B3 add-on image's base: the digest of python:3.15-slim, in the add-on catalog
Websites: each PHP series' image, the digest of php:<series>-apache (sites.php)
Websites: each Node.js version's image, the digest of node:<version>-bookworm-slim (sites.runtimes.node.versions)
Websites: WordPress's image on each PHP series, the digest of wordpress:<version>-php<series>-apache (sites.wordpress; its version moves with .github/scripts/site_app_versions.py)
Websites: wp-cli's image, the digest of wordpress:cli-<version>-php8.4 (sites.wpcli)
Websites: the object cache's image, the digest of valkey:<major>-alpine (sites.object_cache)
Websites: the static sites' image, the digest of nginx-unprivileged:<x.y>-alpine-slim (sites.static)
Websites: the tunnel connector's image, cloudflared's release tag and its digest (sites.tunnel.cloudflare)
Websites: the tunnel image's certificate authorities, the digest of debian:trixie-slim (sites.tunnel.cloudflare.certs)
Websites: the page cache build's base, the digest of caddy:<the proxy's version> (sites.caddy_cache.base)
Websites: the page cache build's builder, the digest of caddy:<the proxy's version>-builder (sites.caddy_cache.builder)
Websites: the npm the Node.js image installs, an exact npm release (sites.runtimes.node.npm)

iw4madmin-release.description: RaidMax/IW4M-Admin's releases with an IW4MAdmin-<build>.zip archive, each with that archive's sha256 (GitHub's asset digest). IW4MAdmin's release workflow marks every release a prerelease; each is one, so each counts as stable here.
transformTemplates: ($zip := function($r) { ($r.assets[$contains(name, /^IW4MAdmin-[0-9.]+\.zip$/) and $contains($string(digest), /^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/)])[0] }; $rel := [$map($$[draft = false and $exists($zip($))], function($r) { ($d := $substringAfter($zip($r).digest, "sha256:"); {"version": $r.tag_name, "releaseTimestamp": $r.published_at, "isStable": true, "digest": $d}) })]; {"releases": $rel})

packageRules.description: Images: the tag's new digest only, never another tag
gcr.io and ghcr.io publish no release timestamp: raise the digest update rather than hold it forever
The fuzz build's base and the two ClusterFuzzLite action images move together
The add-ons' pins are checked every day; B3's fork is this project's own, so its commits need no waiting period
B3's fork: no release-age wait (its releases are this project's own, tagged and signed)
Websites: the site images and npm are checked every day, like the add-ons' pins
Websites: cloudflared's release tag moves too (its version is the release's date, so a new year is not a new major); every other image keeps its tag
Websites: npm stays on its major (a new major may drop a Node.js version the catalog still offers)

The add-ons' and the websites' build files: their pins are the add-on catalog's (custom managers above), and their ARGs have no default. The built-in dockerfile manager reads a tagless ARG BASE_IMAGE digest as the image's latest tag: on B3's it read python:latest and proposed a different Python (#598).
The workflows' actions are Dependabot's: Renovate's built-in github-actions patterns read every workflow, so this manager is off there and reads only the two ClusterFuzzLite action copies
